nodes.label: Capabilities
nodes.rationale: Everything the product-differentiation roadmap adds is a capability: an optional feature the core never depends on. Sign-in, attendance, timetable generation and reports work with every capability off.

nodes.label: Server flag and tenant switch
nodes.rationale: A capability is on only when both the server flag FEATURE_NAME and the tenant capabilities.enabled row are on. The server flag hides the feature for every tenant. The tenant switch defaults to the registry default when no row has been saved. This is the same shape as NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED plus notification_settings.enabled. The capability is checked after the permission check: capabilities decide whether a feature exists, permissions decide who may use it.

nodes.label: Capability fail-closed
nodes.rationale: Missing pieces turn a capability off: no capabilities table, an unknown name, or a lookup error. An install that never visits Settings, Capabilities behaves exactly as before. Registry defaults are on only when on-with-nothing-configured is today's behaviour. Anything that needs a provider, an approval workflow or new data is off by default. Outside an app context, background workers also answer off.

nodes.label: CAPABILITIES registry
nodes.rationale: core.capabilities.CAPABILITIES is the single list: name, title, description, phase, default and a settings schema. The settings page renders from that schema and clean_settings rejects unknown keys. On by default: timetable_preferences, timetable_versions, timetable_grid, calendar_feeds. Off by default: bookings, workload_norms, academic_terms, syllabus, assessments, exams, two_factor, privacy_tools, channels, guardians, attendance_policies.

nodes.label: require_capability route guard
nodes.rationale: The guard answers 404 capability_off when the feature is off. GET /api/session carries the effective map, and the UI hides entries with useCapability, but nothing in the UI can switch a feature on: an API behind the guard still answers 404. New tables must not be referenced by a NOT NULL foreign key from the core schema.

nodes.label: timetable_preferences capability
nodes.rationale: On by default once its revision is applied, because on-with-nothing-configured keeps today's behaviour through built-in weights. Off, the solvers use the legacy objective and no preferences, and the rules and preferences routes answer 404.

nodes.label: timetable_versions capability
nodes.rationale: On by default. The job worker opens a draft only when it is on; otherwise generation replaces live rows directly. keep_drafts bounds how many drafts an institution keeps. An operator who wants the old behaviour switches it off or sets FEATURE_TIMETABLE_VERSIONS false.

nodes.label: bookings capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. Off, room_usage_for_week and booked_room return nothing without touching the table, so the generator, the joint solver and check_slot behave exactly as before. requires_approval defaults to true so requests wait for the room owner's rooms_change_room holders; false approves every clash-free booking at once.

nodes.label: workload_norms capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. Off, limits and assessments are empty, so neither solver sees a norm, the workload_max rule costs nothing, and the workload report keeps its old columns. The norms live in timetable_rules under _workload, with no table of their own. enforce defaults to soft, a cost, rather than a hard constraint.
